verdict.reasoning: Patient reports fever for about seven days with alternating hot, sweaty, and cold episodes: “I've been struggling with fever for the past week… I'm really hot and sweaty all the time” and later “I'm sweating during the night. I'm quite cold… periods of when you're feeling hot and also periods when you're feeling cold as well? Patient: Yes… it's quite interchangeable.”

Diffuse muscle aches: “I'd say that I'm aching all over, really. My muscles are really aching.” Persistent nausea and reduced oral intake: “I'm feeling quite nauseous, so I've not been able to eat very much and I have been drinking, but it's been quite a small amount.” Night sweats and fatigue: “I'm sweating during the night. I'm quite cold.” and “Just generally quite tired and unwell.”

OTC paracetamol and ibuprofen at recommended doses with limited relief: “I've been trying to like take ibuprofen and paracetamol just from over the counter… Just been taking the recommended dose every day of those.” and “it's not really helping… Perhaps slightly, yes, but I'm still experiencing these symptoms, so it does take the edge off of it.”

Denials: “Have you got any cough or cold or sore throat, anything like that? Patient: Not those sort of symptoms really.” Ear pain: “Have you had an ear pain at all? Patient: No, my ears are fine.” Diarrhea: “Have you had any diarrhea? Patient: Not. Not really, no. I'm fine.” Neck stiffness: “Have you got any neck stiffness at all? Patient: No.” Urinary symptoms: “Any problems… when you're passing urine? Patient: No, there's been no problems there… Any painful urination…? Patient: Not at all, no… Are you passing urine more often than normal? Patient: I don't think so, no.” Rash: “Have you got any rash in your body anywhere at all? Patient: I haven't noticed any rashes, no.”

Chronic centralized headache related to screen use and weather: “It's quite centralized over the head.” and “It's something that I've struggled with for years… just related to screen use or like changes in weather patterns, high pressure days.”

Chronic posture-related back pain managed with physiotherapy: “I often have problems with back pain” and “I've been struggling with back pain for quite a while” and “I'm under a physiotherapist at the moment for that… they've said that it's related to long periods of time sitting at a desk and just bad posture.”
Recent Vietnam travel, returned 4 weeks ago: “Have you been abroad anywhere recently? Patient: Yes… I went to Vietnam. I came back four weeks ago now.”

Rural, city, trekking, cycling, and farmland exposure: “we toured to several different parts of the country in the countryside and some cities as well.” and “we were sort of trekking and cycling through farmland and seeing how people lived in their day to day life and in farmland.”

Daily malaria prophylaxis plus a second agent; names unknown: “Did you take malaria preventative medication…? Patient: I did, yes… Was it a weekly tablet or a daily tablet? Doctor notes need to find the cause of fever and mentions concern for malaria and other infections, but does not label it as “fever of unknown origin” nor mention any prior malaria history: “we need to find a reason for why you've got this fever… we need to think about things like malaria or other exotic infections as well.” The term “fever of unknown origin” and “malaria history” are not explicitly stated.

In-person exam in central London clinic: “we're going to need to bring you into one of our clinics [to] exam” and “You can come into one of our clinics in central London. That's one option.”

Planned blood tests including thick and thin films and inflammatory markers: “we're going to need to arrange some blood tests” and “I'll be asking for something called thick and thin blood films to check for malaria and inflammatory markers and things like that.”
Advised not to work until clarified: “But I don't think you can go into work until we've sorted this out, and we need to sort this out sooner rather than later.”
Alternative of local A&E if unable to attend clinic: “if it's inconvenient for you to come into central London because you're living further out, you could actually just attend a local ae.”

Admin will book appointment and patient to call: “What I'm going to do is I will send a message to one of our admin team members asking them to book you in, and if you can, ring the number that I leave in your consultation notes after a few minutes and then they'll slot you in.”
